newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian thermo-electric plant to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Croatian thermo-electric plant to go ahead.

text.p: All conditions have been met for a quick completion of a big thermo-electric plant which is to largely make up for shortage of electricity in Croatia, the state television said on Monday.

Croatian electricity board (HEP) has contracted Austrian Managing Environment, and its consortium partners, electrical firm Siemens and Croatian steelwork producer Djuro Djakovic, to build the Plomin 2 power plant, the head of HEP, Damir Begovic, told HRT television.
"They got the job and I think we now created all pre-conditions for completing the plant," he said.

Earlier this month, HEP and Germany's RWE AG unit RWE Energie electric company agreed to form a joint venture, located on the Adriatic Istrian peninsula, to finance the building of Plomin 2 power plant.
The final value of the joint venture should amount to 500 million marks.
HEP's decision to build Plomin 2, which would be the second coal fired power station in Plomin, sparked fierce protests of Istrian environmentalists and civic organisations in the area.
"Emission of toxic gases into the atmosphere will be minimal. All norms set by Croatian laws will be respected," Begovic said.
The Plomin 2 is designed to reach annual production of 1.3 billion kw/h. The current electricity shortage is covered is by imports totalling $50 million a year.
The HRT said Plomin 2 could be completed by 1998. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
